title: Milestone 3 — admit retries before the deadline, retain late success
subtitle: Baseline: milestone 2. The budget governs retry admission, not callback completion. Both operation time and actual waiting consume the same elapsed budget.

lanes.title: D1 · Stop starting work too late
body: A caller with a deadline wants to avoid starting another retry when the remaining time cannot accommodate its full wait.
A1 seeks this outcome; D2 supplies time-aware admission.

lanes.title: D2 · Admit a retry within budget
body: Today: eligible retries depend only on attempts and delay.
Proposed: also require scheduled and actual retry admission strictly inside a caller-selected elapsed-time budget.

lanes.title: D3 · Full wait must fit
body: After a nonfinal eligible failure, elapsed + next_delay must be strictly less than time_budget.
Equality denies the retry and preserves the current failure. Never shorten a wait to force a retry; protects D1.

lanes.title: D4 · Recheck before retrying
body: After waiting, check elapsed < budget immediately before another call. Check again for zero-delay retries too.
An overshooting wait denies the call. Constrains D2; protects D1.

lanes.title: D5 · Keep an admitted success
body: The first call always runs with a valid clock, even for budget zero. An admitted call may finish after the deadline.
Return a successful result unchanged. A late failure prevents another retry; protects D6.

lanes.title: D6 · Keep useful completed work
body: Callers want the actual result of a successful operation. Milestones 1 and 2 already return that object unchanged.
Budgeting must not turn a completed success into a timeout or discard its result.

lanes.title: A1 · Application author / viewer
body: Today: chooses exception, count, and delay settings.
Proposed: may also choose an elapsed budget. Still owns per-operation timeout and whether repetition is safe.

lanes.title: A2 · Retry Kit
body: Today: admits retries by failure/count alone.
Proposed: ask a per-call budget to admit the next full wait and recheck after waiting. Never interrupt the operation.

lanes.title: A3 · Report operation
body: Runs synchronously and owns its work. The budget does not preempt or cancel it.
The new acceptance fixture consumes 0.4 seconds per read; its second read either succeeds or fails.

lanes.title: A4 · Waiting provider
body: Receives the requested delay and may return later than requested.
The library cannot assume requested wait equals elapsed time. Actual time is observed separately through A5.

lanes.title: A5 · Monotonic clock
body: Default provider: time.monotonic. Tests provide a controlled clock advanced by operation and wait.
Returns finite nondecreasing seconds; its epoch is arbitrary, not a wall-clock timestamp.

lanes.title: A6 · Synchronous process
body: All participants run in the caller’s process. There is no timer interrupt, background monitor, or durable deadline service.
Deadline checks are admission decisions, not hard real-time scheduling guarantees.

lanes.title: C1 · RetryPolicy
body: Today: count, exception, and delay settings.
Proposed: optional time_budget, normalized with the existing finite-duration validator. None disables timing; zero permits only the first call.

lanes.title: C2 · retry executor
body: Today: check attempts, then wait and loop.
Proposed: check attempts first; ask Budget.allows(delay); wait if positive; ask Budget.allows(0); then invoke. Success returns directly.

lanes.title: C3 · Budget
body: No elapsed-time owner exists today.
Proposed: sample a start reading, retain the last reading, and evaluate strict elapsed comparisons. Reject nonfinite or decreasing clock readings.

lanes.title: C4 · Interval iterator
body: Still owns capped doubling, independent of clocks and sleeping.
The budget receives the entire next interval. It can deny the retry, but cannot shorten the wait or alter the doubling rule.

lanes.title: C5 · Controlled-time rehearsal
body: No budget consumer exists today.
Proposed: simulate late success, late failure, exact-deadline denial, and oversleep. The clock advances explicitly; no real sleeping is needed.

lanes.title: C6 · Existing consumer / API
body: Retain the immediate and real-wait scenarios and all previous exports.
The new optional budget and clock parameters preserve behavior for callers leaving the budget unset.

lanes.title: I1 · time_budget=None
body: Optional finite nonnegative int/float seconds; bool is invalid. None means disabled.
Zero is valid: initial success returns, initial failure cannot be retried.

lanes.title: I2 · retry(..., clock=...)
body: Today: operation, policy, waiting function.
Proposed: add keyword-only clock=time.monotonic. Enabled invocations take their own baseline reading immediately before the initial call.

lanes.title: I3 · Budget.allows(delay)
body: Read clock; compute elapsed = now - started. Return elapsed + delay < limit.
Passing delay=0 checks actual admission time after waiting. No absolute deadline addition is needed.

lanes.title: I4 · operation() → result/error
body: Success returns directly, with no post-success budget veto. Eligible failure enters admission checks; unrelated failure escapes.
Only operation failures qualify for retry matching.

lanes.title: I5 · clock() → seconds
body: Called only when a budget is enabled. Samples finite, nondecreasing numeric seconds.
Clock exceptions and invalid readings escape as dependency failures, even if their classes are retryable for the operation.

lanes.title: I6 · wait(seconds)
body: Only full positive intervals that fit are passed to the waiting provider. Zero delays do not call it.
A waiting failure still escapes. Actual elapsed time is re-read after a successful wait.

lanes.title: S1 · Optional budget setting
body: Immutable policy duration reused across calls. None adds no timing state and causes no clock reads.
It is not an absolute wall-clock deadline or a shared countdown.

lanes.title: S2 · Per-invocation timing
body: Budget retains started and last readings. Each invocation gets a new baseline.
Count, schedule, and timing remain local even when a policy is reused.

lanes.title: S3 · Prospective elapsed time
body: Derived from now - started + full delay. Operation duration and actual prior waits are already included in now.
Only a value strictly below the limit permits waiting.

lanes.title: S4 · Last operation failure
body: Active exception remains in the executor’s handler through both budget gates and the wait.
Either gate denies with a bare re-raise; no synthetic timeout exception replaces it.

lanes.title: S5 · Admitted running call
body: Once invoked, the callback owns execution until it returns or raises. The library keeps no interruptible task handle.
A late success is still a valid result; an individual call can exceed the entire budget.

lanes.title: S6 · Controlled test time
body: A fresh clock fixture records readings/waits and advances on explicit operation or waiting steps.
Exact boundary tests use binary-exact values. Decimal scenario values are checked with appropriate numeric assertions.

lanes.title: V1 · Configuration checks
body: Reject negative/nonfinite budgets and bool. Accept None and zero.
Retain the 63 passing pre-budget checks and all existing duration validation rules.

lanes.title: V2 · One-second acceptance
body: Read 1 fails at 0.4; wait 0.3; read 2 starts at 0.7 and finishes at 1.1.
Success returns; failure preserves read 2’s exception. Both have two calls and one requested wait.

lanes.title: V3 · Exact admission boundary
body: Elapsed 0.5 plus wait 0.5 with budget 1.0: deny without waiting. An inside value admits; an outside value denies.
Use exact binary fractions to distinguish strict comparison from tolerance-based behavior.

lanes.title: V4 · Oversleep / zero delay
body: A wait returning at or beyond the deadline causes no next call. Recheck even when requested delay is zero.
Budget zero still permits the first call, but never a retry.

lanes.title: V5 · Dependency / reuse checks
body: Disabled budget reads no clock. Enabled clock failures, nonfinite readings, or backwards time escape.
Reused policies get fresh baselines; large clock epochs do not become absolute deadline sums.

lanes.title: V6 · Installed consumers
body: Run both report examples from an installed wheel. The new controlled-time consumer prints four deterministic outcomes.
Full suite retains the prior real-wait consumer and every attempt/failure guarantee.
